_note: Read by installer/prepare.ps1, checked by tests/test_installer.py, and HEAD-verified by .github/workflows/installer.yml. Every field matters: bytes catches a captive portal or a proxy error page arriving as a successful download, sha256 catches the asset being replaced. Refresh both together, never one alone.

python.refresh: Download the installer from www.python.org over HTTPS and hash it. python.org publishes no .sha256 sidecar, so the pin records what was fetched rather than what a vendor asserts. 3.14 is what the author's deployment runs and what a CI leg exercises; the floor stays 3.9 and any Python already on the machine is used as it is, so this version only ever reaches a machine that had none.

ffmpeg.refresh: gyan.dev publishes a .sha256 sidecar beside every versioned package, so the hash and the size can be read without downloading 111 MB: fetch <url>.sha256 and read Content-Length. But do download it once per bump and run temp/check_pins.py, because two fields here cannot be read off a sidecar: binaries, which is the folder name inside the zip, and whether the build still has NVENC. Both were measured on this pin rather than believed. Use the versioned packages/ path, never ffmpeg-release-essentials.zip: that one moves, and a pin against a moving target fails at the next vendor release.
ffmpeg.verified: 2026-08-18: sha256 and bytes match the downloaded file; the archive holds one top-level folder; ffmpeg.exe reports 9.0.1 and lists av1_nvenc, h264_nvenc and hevc_nvenc, built with --enable-nvenc, --enable-cuda-llvm, --enable-libx264 and --enable-libx265. Those are the three encoders detect_encoders() probes for.
